notes: Two disconnected groups is correct for this set, so I kept it. Set 8159-1 contains two separate cars that the booklet never joins. The pages say so directly. Page 3 shows bag 1 making only the yellow Racer X car and bag 2 making only the red Taejo Togokhan car. Pages 4-17 build the yellow car and pages 18-30 build the red car, each ending in its own finished model. The yellow car is b1-b113 and the red car is b114-b228. Connecting them would invent a join that does not exist in the instructions.

Within each car, all pieces are connected. The yellow car's rear chassis and floor are joined through b16, which rests on b1, b2, b29 and b30. The red car's rear chassis, floor and front chassis are joined through b137. Wheels, tyres, bushes, hinges, the sideways plate and the sticker sheet are connected by other_joins.
Every rests_on was checked against the catalogue ports. No piece rests on a part with no studs (arches, inverted slopes, curved 3x1 bricks, tiles).

The minifigure parts (heads, helmets, torsos, legs) are not in the parts list, so they are not recorded. The sticker sheet (b70) is recorded as one piece and attached to the yellow car by an other_join.
The page images are small, so rests_on for many mid-build pieces is my best inference. The piece counts and types match the parts list exactly (228 pieces).

Hinge top plates (b188, b189) have no anti-studs. They connect only through the hinge to the white bases b186 and b187. The wheel cover 62359 appears only on the yellow car. Each axle (3707) runs through the pin holes of Technic bricks and carries a wheel at each end. Each wheel has a tyre, and a bush sits on each axle end.

notes: Set 8159-1 contains two cars. Pieces b1-b113 are the yellow Racer X car (bag 1). Pieces b114-b228 are the red Taejo Togokhan car (bag 2). The total is 228 pieces and each type matches the parts list.
The minifigure parts (heads, helmets, torsos, legs) are not in the parts list, so they are not recorded. The sticker sheet (b70) is recorded as one piece.

Both cars are built from sub-assemblies: a rear chassis, a floor, and a front chassis, which are then joined and covered with body panels. The page images are small and some views are ambiguous, so rests_on for many mid-build pieces is my best inference. The piece counts and types are certain.
The floor plates (b16, b137) are recorded as clutching the free ends of the chassis arm plates. The front chassis arms rest under the floor.
The two hinge top plates (b188, b189) have no anti-studs. They connect only through the hinge to the white hinge bases (b186, b187), so their rests_on is empty.
The wheel cover (62359) appears only on the yellow car. The red car's wheels have no cover.
Technic bricks hold the axles (3707) through their pin holes. Each axle carries a wheel at each end, with a tyre on each wheel and a bush on the axle end.
Where several parts share one stud row, I listed the nearest supporting part. This covers the wheel arches, curved slopes, tiles and plates.

Yellow car (the dashboard slope, floor bricks and the other early parts) is recorded in the order of its steps. The pieces in b47-b95 for the yellow car's upper deck, hood and stripes are inferred from the final pictures.
